04/Dated: 18th October, 2022 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Pursuant to the order dated 24.08.2022 notices were issued to the petitioners.

A service report has been received indicating therein that petitioner no. 1, namely- Babulal Ram has died and the notice has been served upon the petitioner no.2.
3.
In view of the aforesaid fact, the instant application is dismissed as abated against the petitioner no. 1, namely- Babulal Ram.

4. This revision application is directed against the judgment dated 28.11.2006, passed by learned VI Additional Sessions Judge (F.T.C.) Dhanbad, in Cr. Appeal No. 107 of 1993/40 of 2003; whereby the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 03.09.1993 passed by learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Dhanbad, in P.F.A. Case No. 2 of 1991, corresponding to Trial No. 1039 of 1993;
whereby the petitioners were convicted under sections 16 (i)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and were sentenced to undergo R.I. for one year and a fine of Rs. 1,000/-, and in default of payment of fine the convicts were further directed to undergo S.I. for 1 year.
Babulal Ram vs The State Of Jharkhand.

Learned appellate court reduced the sentence of R.I. from 1 year to 6 months and sustained the fine amount and appeal filed by the petitioner was dismissed with modification in sentence.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner fairly confines his argument on the question of sentence on the ground that the instant case is of the year 1991 and about 31 years have elapsed since then and the petitioner must have suffered the mental agony for ongoing litigation.

He further submits that the petitioner no.2 remained in custody for about 18 days and has never misused the privilege of bail and he is not a habitual offender and is the only earing member of his family, as such some leniency may be granted by this Court and sentence may be modified to period already undergone.
6.

Learned Addl.P.P. opposes the contention of the petitioner and submits that there is concurrent finding and as such, no interference is required.
7.

After going through the impugned judgments including the lower court records and keeping in mind the limited submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner and also the scope of revision jurisdiction, I am not inclined to interfere with the finding of the courts below and as such the judgment of conviction passed by the learned trial court and upheld by the learned appellate court is, hereby, sustained.
8.

However, so far as sentence is concerned, it is apparent from record that the incident is of the year 1991 and 31 years have elapsed and the petitioner no.2 must have suffered the rigors of litigation for the last 31 years.
He also remained in custody for about 18 days and has never misused the privilege of bail.
Further, he is the sole earning member of his family and sending him back to prison at this stage will hamper the entire family.
In addition, the incident does not reflect any cruelty on the part of the petitioner or any mental depravity.

9. In a situation of this nature, I am of the opinion that no fruitful purpose would be served by sending the petitioner/convict back to prison; rather interest of justice would be sufficed if the sentence is modified to period already undergone.

10. Thus, the sentence passed by the learned trial Court and upheld by the learned appellate Court is hereby further modified to the extent that the petitioner no.2 is sentenced to undergo for the period already undergone.
11. With the aforesaid observations, and modification in sentence only, the instant criminal revision application stands disposed of.
12. The petitioner shall be discharged from the liability of his bail bond.

13. Let a copy of this order be communicated to the courts below and also to the petitioner through the officer- in-charge of concerned police station.
14.
Let the lower court record be sent to the court concerned forthwith.
Babulal Ram vs The State Of Jharkhand.
